candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes a patient with icterus, upper abdominal pain, elevated bilirubin, hepatobiliary enzymes, HbA1c of 7.2%, elevated CEA and CA19-9, and imaging findings (diffusely enlarged, sausage-shaped pancreas with delayed enhancement and capsule-like rim, intrahepatic bile-duct dilation, diffuse pancreatic enlargement with low T1, slightly high T2, high DWI signal, diffuse FDG uptake in pancreas and hypermetabolic lymph nodes, stenosis of lower bile duct, diffuse narrowing of main pancreatic duct). While some imaging findings (sausage-shaped pancreas, capsule-like rim) can be seen in autoimmune pancreatitis, the elevated tumor markers (CEA, CA19-9), elevated HbA1c (suggesting new-onset diabetes), and hypermetabolic lymph nodes on PET are more indicative of malignancy, specifically pancreatic adenocarcinoma, as per the reference. Autoimmune pancreatitis type 2 is a distinct inflammatory condition with a different pathogenesis and typically normal tumor markers.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: The candidate specifies autoimmune pancreatitis type 2, which is a different etiology than the reference's adenocarcinoma.
